🇨🇦🇨🇦🇨🇦
There was a French film Taxi 3. In it, a police commissioner gathers a meeting and starts solemnly with the phrase:
“Gentlemen, we are in deep shit!”
So, I wanted to share some Canadian demographic statistics.
1. In 2024, the fertility rate dropped to a record low — 1.25 children per woman.
For comparison, in the 1950s in Canada there were about 4 children per woman.
But the next generation, in the 1970s, was already producing only 1.7 children.
This likely coincides with the “freedom” (or rather, unhinged permissiveness) in the West that young people gained around 1968.
2. This is where you’ll understand why I remembered the commissioner from the movie.
97% of Canada’s population growth comes from immigration.
By 2032, it is expected that 100% of population growth will come from immigration.
3. Currently, 23%, or 8.4 million, of Canada’s total population are immigrants.
Of these:
10.7% are from India
8.6% from the Philippines
8.6% from China
Since 1971, immigration from Europe has declined from 61.6% to 10.1% (by 2021).
Asia now accounts for 62% of immigration.
4. In 2024, 42.3% of newborns were born to foreign-born mothers.
(Remember that immigrants make up 23% of the population, and women are only about half of that.
So even if we assume 12% immigrant women, they account for over 42% of all births.)
5. The average age in Canada is 41.
People of European origin are significantly older than immigrants.
6. Canada currently has more people aged 65+ (8.1 million, or 19% of the population)
than children under 14 (6.3 million, or 15%).
7. Households:
29.3% — single-person households
25.6% — couples without children
25.3% — couples with children
The share of people aged 35–44 living alone is 10% (it was 5% in 1981).
35.1% of young people aged 20–34 live with their parents.
8. The number of non-religious people in Canada continues to decline.
Over the past 20 years, it dropped from 34.6% to 16.5% of the total population.
Today, there are 12.6 million religious people out of 41.5 million.
The number of Christians has declined from 77.1% to 53.3% since the beginning of the century.
9. Religious breakdown:
Jews: 335,000 or 0.8% of the population (1.1% in 2001)
Islam: 1.8 million or 4.9% (about 2% a quarter-century ago)
Hindus: 2.3%
Sikhs: 2.1%
Christians: 53.3%
Atheists: 34.6%
10. Of all working people in Canada, 21.8% are aged 55–64.
They’ll be retiring soon.
We’re screwed.
11. The number of immigrants without citizenship or permanent resident status is about
2.87 million people, or 7% of Canada’s population.
